title: A, An and The: Choosing the Right Article
summary: Use a/an to introduce one non-specific person or thing and the when the listener can identify which one you mean. Learn how previous mentions, shared situations and unique descriptions affect your choice.
learningObjectives: Choose a or an when introducing one unspecified singular countable noun.
Use the for a person or thing already identified in the conversation.
Use the when the setting makes the intended person or thing clear.
Choose the with unique descriptions and superlative forms.

explanation.heading: Introduce one person or thing with a/an
explanation.body: Use a or an with a singular countable noun when you mean one person or thing, but not a particular one already known to the listener. Choose an before a vowel sound and a before a consonant sound. The noun may be new to the conversation.
explanation.example: I saw an unusual bird near the river.

explanation.heading: Use the for a person or thing already mentioned
explanation.body: After you introduce something, use the when you refer to that same thing again. A/an introduces it; the helps your listener recognise which one you mean. This also works when the listener already knows the particular item.
explanation.example: We bought a small lamp. The lamp is beside the sofa.

explanation.heading: Use the when the situation identifies the item
explanation.body: You can say the even on a first mention when the situation makes the item clear. In a shared room, the light may mean that room’s light. In a home, the bathroom may be the bathroom you both know. The speaker and listener need to understand which one is meant.
explanation.example: Please leave your coat in the hall.

explanation.heading: Use the when the description picks out one
explanation.body: Use the when the description identifies a unique item in the context, such as the only lift in a building or the captain of a particular team. Superlatives such as the youngest and the cheapest normally take the. A/an remains possible for one of several people or things.
explanation.example: This is the quietest room in the hotel.

left.label: Introducing an item
left.example: I found a notebook on the train.
left.note: A notebook introduces one unspecified notebook.

right.label: Identifying that item
right.example: The notebook has a green cover.
right.note: The notebook refers to the same notebook already mentioned.

comparisons.title: Any suitable item or one specific item

left.label: One of several
left.example: Could you bring me a cup?

right.label: A known item
right.example: Could you bring me the blue cup?
right.note: Blue identifies which particular cup is wanted.

examples.sentence: We saw a bicycle outside the shop, and the bicycle had a yellow seat.
examples.note: The second reference identifies the bicycle introduced earlier.

examples.sentence: There is an art gallery near my office.
examples.note: An introduces one gallery that is not already identified.

examples.sentence: Could you open the fridge, please?
examples.note: The shared kitchen makes the fridge identifiable.

examples.sentence: Jade is the oldest player on our team.
examples.note: The is used before a superlative.

examples.sentence: I need a map, but I cannot find the map you lent me.
examples.note: A map means any map; the map you lent me means a particular one.

commonMistakes.incorrect: I saw a owl near the fence.
commonMistakes.correct: I saw an owl near the fence.
commonMistakes.why: Owl starts with a vowel sound, so use an.

commonMistakes.incorrect: Leo bought a new backpack. A backpack is black.
commonMistakes.correct: Leo bought a new backpack. The backpack is black.
commonMistakes.why: The second mention refers to the backpack already introduced.

commonMistakes.incorrect: Could you close door to the garden?
commonMistakes.correct: Could you close the door to the garden?
commonMistakes.why: The description identifies a specific door.

commonMistakes.incorrect: This is a cheapest ticket for the concert.
commonMistakes.correct: This is the cheapest ticket for the concert.
commonMistakes.why: Superlatives such as cheapest normally take the.

studyTips: Ask whether you are introducing one item or identifying an item already known to both speakers.
When choosing between a and an, listen to the first sound of the next word rather than only looking at its first letter.
Look for clues such as earlier mentions, a shared room, only one, and superlatives.

exercises.prompt: Last night I saw ___ owl in a tree. I had never seen it before.
exercises.feedback: Owl begins with a vowel sound. An introduces one bird for the first time.

exercises.prompt: I borrowed a bicycle from Ella. ___ bicycle has a small basket.
exercises.feedback: The bicycle identifies the particular bicycle mentioned in the first sentence.

exercises.prompt: This village has only one post office. Where is ___ post office?
exercises.feedback: The post office is identifiable because the village has only one.

exercises.prompt: Mina is ___ youngest member of our music group.
exercises.feedback: The is normally used with superlatives such as youngest.

exercises.prompt: We need ___ chair for our new desk. Any comfortable chair will do. (Write a, an or the.)
acceptedAnswers: a
exercises.feedback: A chair means one unspecified chair; chair begins with a consonant sound.

exercises.prompt: I found a scarf on the bus. ___ scarf is red. (Write a, an or the.)
acceptedAnswers: the
exercises.feedback: The refers back to the particular scarf in the first sentence.

exercises.prompt: Our flat has one balcony door. Please open ___ balcony door. (Write a, an or the.)
acceptedAnswers: the
exercises.feedback: There is only one balcony door in this flat, so the listener knows which one.

exercises.prompt: Lena wants to become ___ architect. (Write a, an or the.)
acceptedAnswers: an
exercises.feedback: Architect begins with a vowel sound, so use an for one profession.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: I saw a old bicycle outside the café.
acceptedAnswers: I saw an old bicycle outside the café.
exercises.feedback: Use an before old because it begins with a vowel sound.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: We found a dog in the park. A dog was very friendly.
acceptedAnswers: We found a dog in the park. The dog was very friendly.
exercises.feedback: On the second mention, the identifies the same dog.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: This flat has only one bathroom. Please clean a bathroom before the guests arrive.
acceptedAnswers: This flat has only one bathroom. Please clean the bathroom before the guests arrive.
exercises.feedback: There is only one bathroom in the flat, so use the.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: This is a cheapest train ticket available.
acceptedAnswers: This is the cheapest train ticket available.
exercises.feedback: Cheapest is a superlative, normally used with the.

speakingExercises.prompt: Say that you bought one umbrella yesterday. Begin with “I bought”.
acceptedAnswers: I bought an umbrella yesterday.
speakingExercises.feedback: An is used because umbrella begins with a vowel sound.

speakingExercises.prompt: You bought a red hat. Say the same hat is on your bed. Begin with “The hat”.
acceptedAnswers: The hat is on my bed.
speakingExercises.feedback: The identifies the hat that has already been mentioned.

speakingExercises.prompt: Say that Ella is the youngest member of the team. Begin with “Ella”.
acceptedAnswers: Ella is the youngest member of the team.
speakingExercises.feedback: Use the with the superlative youngest.

speakingExercises.prompt: You see a blue notebook on a shelf for the first time. Say so in one sentence, beginning with 'There is' and ending with 'on the shelf'.
acceptedAnswers: There is a blue notebook on the shelf.
There's a blue notebook on the shelf.
speakingExercises.feedback: Use a before blue notebook to introduce one new, unspecified countable item.

speakingExercises.prompt: You found one small boat. In these two sentences, correct only the article in the second sentence so it means the same boat: 'I found a small boat. A boat was empty.' Say both sentences.
acceptedAnswers: I found a small boat. The boat was empty.
speakingExercises.feedback: The boat refers back to the boat introduced in the first sentence.

speakingExercises.prompt: You and a friend are in a room with only one window. Ask your friend to open it. Begin with 'Could you open' and finish with 'please'.
acceptedAnswers: Could you open the window, please?
speakingExercises.feedback: The window identifies the only window in the shared room.

speakingExercises.prompt: A friend says 'I need the pencil', but any pencil will do. Correct only the article and say the whole sentence.
acceptedAnswers: I need a pencil.
speakingExercises.feedback: A pencil means any one suitable pencil; the pencil would identify a particular one.

speakingExercises.prompt: A house has three bedrooms, and the blue bedroom is the quietest. Make one sentence starting 'The blue bedroom' and ending with the exact words 'the quietest room in the house'.
acceptedAnswers: The blue bedroom is the quietest room in the house.
speakingExercises.feedback: Use the with the superlative quietest when identifying one room in a group.

listeningExercises.audioText: I noticed a small cat outside, and the cat followed me home.
listeningExercises.prompt: Which phrase refers to the same animal after its first mention?
listeningExercises.feedback: The cat is the second reference to the cat already introduced.

listeningExercises.audioText: Please put the keys on the kitchen table before you leave.
listeningExercises.prompt: Where should the keys be put?
listeningExercises.feedback: The kitchen table identifies the place named by the speaker.

listeningExercises.audioText: There is an envelope under your notebook.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the article heard immediately before “envelope”.
acceptedAnswers: an
listeningExercises.feedback: An is used before the vowel sound at the beginning of envelope.

listeningExercises.audioText: I bought a small camera at the market. The camera still works, so I'll take pictures with it.
listeningExercises.prompt: What will the speaker use to take pictures?
choices: A camera bought at the market
listeningExercises.feedback: The camera is the same working camera the speaker introduced with a small camera.

listeningExercises.audioText: This building has two lifts, but only the lift by the main door goes to the top floor.
listeningExercises.prompt: Which lift can take someone to the highest floor?
choices: The lift by the main entrance
The lift far from the main door
listeningExercises.feedback: Only the lift by the main door goes to the top floor; the description identifies that particular lift.

listeningExercises.audioText: Please do not take the red plate. You can use any white plate for your lunch.
listeningExercises.feedback: The red plate is a particular plate to avoid, but any white plate is acceptable.

listeningExercises.audioText: I found a small key this morning. The key opens the garden gate.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the article you hear before the second mention of the object that was found.
acceptedAnswers: the
listeningExercises.feedback: The is used on the second mention because the listener now knows which key is meant.

listeningExercises.audioText: An excellent guide showed us the way to the museum.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the article heard immediately before the adjective describing the guide.
acceptedAnswers: an
listeningExercises.feedback: An comes before excellent because the next word begins with a vowel sound.
